segments.text:
Verſ. 2.
Wherefore is thine apparell red, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the wine preſſe?

HE proſecutes the ſame argument. But becauſe the bare recitall would not haue been of ſufficient weight, therefore he doth not at once manifeſt from whence this red colour in Gods garments did proceede, but rather continues his Interrogation ſtill, that he might the better rouze vp their ſpirits, to the conſideration of ſo rare & vnwonted a thing. For his meaning is to ſay, that this ſprinkling with blood is a matter extraordinarie, and not ſeene before. And therefore the ſimilitude of the preſſer of grapes, ſutes very well. For Bozrah,
which hee mentioned in the firſt verſe, was ſituated in a countrie of vines: as if he would haue ſaid, the grape gatherings ſhal be much differing frō the old wont: for blood, in ſtead of the iuice of grapes, ſhall now bee ſquezed out.
